newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's revered Friar Damiao dies aged 98.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's revered Friar Damiao dies aged 98.

text.p: A friar who was revered by millions of Catholic worshippers in Brazil's impoverished northeast died on Saturday, aged 98.

Friar Damiao, born as Pio Gianotti in 1898 in the Italian city of Bozzano, was declared dead after his heart and lungs ceased to function, said an official at a hospital in the coastal city of Recife, Pernambuco state.
The Capuchin friar was hospitalized earlier this month and declared brain dead May 27, the official said.

Hundreds of Damiao's followers outside the hospital sang hymns and waved photographs of the diminutive, bearded Franciscan. Over decades, he criss-crossed the vast, arid northeast to preach his fiery sermons.

He repeatedly said hell was waiting for adulterers, communists, women who used birth control or wore short skirts. In his view, even people who enjoyed to dance, one of the region's favourite pastimes, were damned.
Damiao was banned from preaching in several cities by bishops opposed to his views. But his unflagging drive to bring the Bible to Brazil's most remote backlands endeared him to the people.

Old age eventually prevented him from preaching. But helpers continued to bear him through towns and villages where thousands of worshippers would typically gather in the streets in the hope of kissing his hand or his drooping head.
